title: MRP-VM
targetDuration: 1–2 minutes; hard maximum 120 seconds after measured voice timing

scenes.title: Brilliant once, unreliable tomorrow
scenes.viewerPurpose: A good answer may not be repeatable. A proposed architecture turns single successful answers into versioned, testable and accountable organizational capabilities.
scenes.composition: A scientist returns to yesterday’s useful answer beside a calendar that has moved forward. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: A scientist returns to yesterday’s useful answer beside a calendar that has moved forward.
Show the colleague asking for the method behind the result, with that space still empty.

cues.text: Your AI gives a brilliant answer today, but nobody can reproduce it tomorrow.
cues.visualAction: A scientist returns to yesterday’s useful answer beside a calendar that has moved forward.
cues.emotion: Warm recognition; gently emphasize “tomorrow”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: MRP-VM proposes turning successful AI work into repeatable procedures that a team can inspect, test, and control.
cues.visualAction: Show the colleague asking for the method behind the result, with that space still empty.
cues.emotion: Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “repeatable procedures”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.

scenes.title: The conditions of good work
scenes.viewerPurpose: Success may rely on conditions nobody recorded. The inquiry goes beyond the visible answer.
scenes.composition: Expose a missing source or instruction beside the retained answer. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.

cues.text: A useful response may depend on forgotten instructions, temporary sources, or an expert's invisible intervention.
cues.visualAction: Expose a missing source or instruction beside the retained answer.
cues.emotion: Curious caution; gently emphasize “forgotten instructions”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: The book examines the procedures, evidence, and permissions behind a good result.

cues.emotion: Patient clarity; gently emphasize “behind a good result”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

scenes.title: A change that earns trust
scenes.viewerPurpose: The proposed design keeps improvement reviewable. Tests and histories make responsibility more concrete.

cues.text: Tests, version histories, and clear responsibilities turn model changes into decisions people can examine.

scenes.title: From answer to capability
scenes.viewerPurpose: A team needs more than a fortunate result. Repetition creates a specific reason to read.

cues.text: For teams moving beyond experiments, the question is whether good work can survive its lucky beginning.

cues.text: Begin with an answer that worked once, and ask what it would take to rely on it again.
